title: ₹40 Crore to Retire in India? Why That Viral Number Is Not Yours
meta_title: ₹40 Crore to Retire in India? Why It Is Not Your Number
subtitle: The viral ₹40 crore number is a future projection built for one expensive lifestyle, not a universal target. Here is where it came from, why inflation drives almost all of it, and how to find your own real number.
description: The viral ₹40 crore retirement number for India explained in plain terms: where it came from, why it is a future value projection resting on a 9% inflation assumption, why it is almost certainly not your number, and how to calculate what you actually need.
toast: ₹40 crore is a projection for one expensive life 20 years out, and your own number depends entirely on what you spend.
If you have ₹1 crore today, compounding at 10% quietly hands you ₹17 crore in 30 years.

faqs.question: Do you really need ₹40 crore to retire in India?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, unless you already live a very expensive life. The ₹40 crore figure is a future projection for someone spending ₹2 lakh a month today, grown at 9% lifestyle inflation over 20 years and funded across a 30 year retirement. Your own number depends on your own spending, and someone spending ₹50,000 a month today arrives at a corpus closer to ₹7 crore under the same framework.

faqs.question: Where did the ₹40 crore retirement figure come from?
faqs.answer: It came from Sandeep Jethwani, a co-founder of the wealth management firm Dezerv, on The Money Mindset podcast with Sonia Shenoy. The example took someone aged 40 spending ₹2 lakh a month, grew that spending at about 9% a year to roughly ₹11.2 lakh a month by age 60, and funded that across a 30 year retirement, which works out to about ₹40 crore.

faqs.question: How much do you actually need to retire in India?
faqs.answer: Start from your own numbers rather than a headline. Take your current annual spending, your retirement age, how long you need the money to last, the inflation you honestly expect, and the real return your portfolio should earn, then work backwards. Two people in the same city can end up with completely different numbers, which is exactly how it should be.

faqs.question: Why does ₹40 crore sound so much higher than American FIRE numbers?
faqs.answer: Because it is measured in nominal rupees in the year 2046 and people compared it against dollars you would spend today, which is not a fair comparison. It also uses a 9% inflation assumption, while typical American FIRE examples assume around 3%. It is a comparison problem, not proof that India is more expensive than the United States.
